title: Sell Mineral Rights in Beallsville, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Beallsville, PA | Route 88
metaDescription: Beallsville mineral owners on Route 88: see how post-production deductions hit your royalty and get a straightforward cash offer.
heroLead: Route 88 runs right through Beallsville, and so does the boundary of at least a couple of Marcellus spacing units drilled over the last decade.
intro: Beallsville is a small borough on the Route 88 corridor south of Washington, in a part of the county that's been leased and drilled steadily since the Marcellus rush started. If you own minerals here, odds are you or your family signed a lease sometime in the 2000s or early 2010s, when landmen were working this stretch hard, and you've been collecting a royalty ever since, however it's shrunk or shifted over the years.
We sold our own family's minerals once, so we know exactly what it feels like to stare at a royalty statement and not trust the number at the bottom. That's the whole reason we do this differently.

sections.heading: The deduction line nobody explained when you signed
paragraphs: Most leases signed in this area during the boom years included standard language allowing the operator to deduct post-production costs, gathering, compression, processing, and transportation, before calculating your royalty. Under Pennsylvania's Kilmer v. Elexco ruling, that deduction is legal even when the lease describes your royalty as a share of gross proceeds, which is exactly the kind of fine print that makes owners feel like the rules changed on them after the fact.
If you've watched your Beallsville royalty check shrink even during periods when gas prices held steady, post-production costs stacking on top of natural well decline is usually the answer.

sections.heading: Held by production and what that means for you
paragraphs: Once a well on your unit is producing, your lease is typically held by production indefinitely, meaning the operator's rights don't expire the way they would under an unproduced primary term. That's good for stability but it also means you can't simply wait out the lease to renegotiate better terms; the interest you sell today reflects the lease you're already locked into.

sections.heading: What we check before making an offer
paragraphs: We pull your deed and lease history through the Washington County Recorder of Deeds, confirm your net mineral acreage and decimal interest in the unit, and review whatever royalty statements you can send us. That's what the offer is built on, not a guess.

faqs.question: Why did my royalty check drop even though gas prices didn't fall much?
faqs.answer: Natural well decline plus stacked post-production deductions is the most common cause. Wells produce their strongest volumes early and taper off, so the deduction line takes a bigger relative bite as gross volume shrinks.

faqs.question: Can I sell just my Beallsville tract and keep minerals elsewhere?
faqs.answer: Yes. We evaluate and price interests tract by tract, so you can sell one holding and keep another.

faqs.question: Is my Route 88 property definitely held by production?
faqs.answer: We'll confirm that for you by checking the well records and unit designation tied to your specific parcel before we finalize an offer.
